clue.text: New York gang includes small kids

indicators.note: the gang name holds the next piece within it, the way a group includes a member

parts.note: the Jets are the New York street gang in West Side Story
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A New York street gang is joined by some little children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' looks like a noun for children, but it is the verb: teases or jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to tease or joke with them, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Islanders endlessly paid to fill preserve containers

indicators.note: the letters go inside the containers, filling them

parts.note: jam cans would be containers for jam, a fruit preserve

indicators.note: without its ends, the word keeps only its middle letters

explanation.surface: Islanders are paid, without end, to fill jars of preserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips the first and last letters of 'paid'; 'to fill' sets what remains inside the containers.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the Caribbean island of Jamaica are islanders.

clue.text: Cut peel of squash and beetroot

indicators.note: the peel is the outer skin, so the first and last letters

parts.note: beetroot is a deep red colour

explanation.surface: Kitchen directions: cut the skin off the squash and the beetroot.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear or cut into thin strips is to cut something up finely.

clue.text: Inflated wheel, oddly, to go in wheel-less conveyance

indicators.note: the odd letters are put inside the conveyance

parts.note: a sled runs on runners, not wheels

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A pumped-up wheel, strangely, is fitted to a vehicle that has no wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes W, E, L from WHEEL, put inside SLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something puffed up with air has grown bigger, been blown up.

clue.text: Report of perfume demonstration at focal location

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase that follows is said aloud

parts.note: a perfume is a scent, and a demonstration is a rally, a mass protest meeting

explanation.surface: A news report about a protest march over a fragrance, held in the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Say SCENT RALLY and it sounds like the adverb meaning in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed in the middle, at the focal point, is positioned in a central way.

clue.text: Herbs beginning to cause rash

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its first letter

parts.note: hives is an itchy skin rash, urticaria

explanation.surface: Some herbs start to give people a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Small onion-family plants with hollow leaves used in cooking are herbs.

clue.text: Near agreement to set up retirement drink

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means put upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: An agreement nearly arranged for a drink at someone's retirement party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work, but it is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink taken just before bed, when retiring for the night.

clue.text: Hates concerning learner beset by struggles

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the learner goes inside

parts.note: vies means competes, struggles
L is the learner plate on a car

explanation.surface: Someone hates this, a learner being surrounded by difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset by' signals the learner going inside the struggles; strictly the answer means abuses verbally, so 'Hates' is a loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking of someone with contempt and abuse shows loathing, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Yearlong travels around Italy for soldier

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the other piece
the letters travel about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A year-long journey around Italy, made by a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travels' rearranges YEARLONG to LEGONARY; 'around' puts it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman foot soldier serving in a legion, so a soldier of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Produce that is left in yard

indicators.note: the pieces go into the other piece

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Produce, that is, which has been left in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' looks like a noun for crops but is the verb, to give or bring forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring forth a crop or a return, as a field or an investment does, is to generate it.

clue.text: Grant Mike dubious promotion

indicators.note: dubious letters are suspect, not to be trusted as they stand, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Grant Mike appears to be receiving a questionable promotion at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion' looks like a job advancement, but it is the selling sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion of a product, advertising and selling it, is the business of the sales and advertising department.

clue.text: European Union almost provided backing? It's unclear

indicators.note: going backwards, so the assembled letters are read from the end
almost means the word is not quite complete, dropping its last letter

parts.note: provided means gave, supplied

explanation.surface: A query over whether the EU nearly gave its support, and the answer is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts GAVE to GAV; 'backing' turns EUGAV round.
explanation.definitionFit: Vague and unclear are synonyms: both mean imprecise or ill-defined.

clue.text: Find adult aged shunning all outsiders and humour

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its outer letters, keeping only the inside

explanation.surface: Someone is told to find an old grown-up who avoids strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humour' is the verb, to go along with someone's wishes; FIND, ADULT and AGED lose their outer letters to leave IN, DUL and GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To humour someone is to give in to their whims, a synonym for pampering them.

clue.text: Engineer cross after permit is rejected

indicators.note: the crossing piece comes after the other one
something rejected is sent back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to permit is to let
a ford is a place to cross a river; to ford is to cross

explanation.surface: Instructions to cross a road once permission has been refused.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Telford was a Scottish civil engineer, famed for roads, canals and bridges; a Shropshire new town bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Telford was a celebrated 18th–19th century builder of bridges and canals, an example of an engineer.

clue.text: What happens when PM begins making reforms

definitions.meaning: the morning, a.m., finishes when the afternoon, p.m., starts
makes changes for the better, corrects

explanation.surface: A description of what happens when a new Prime Minister starts making changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like the Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem: when afternoon starts, the a.m. is over, read as AM ENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform something is to correct or improve it, which is what this verb means, as in altering a text.

clue.text: Lucerne redeveloped to house very big arena

indicators.note: the rearranged letters house, or contain, the other piece
redeveloped means rebuilt in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OS means outsize, very big

explanation.surface: Lucerne is being rebuilt to provide a huge stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucerne is a Swiss city; 'redeveloped' rearranges it to ENCLURE, holding OS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fenced-off area, such as at a racecourse, is an arena of a kind.

clue.text: Machine part chap must regularly handle

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one, starting with the first

parts.note: a haft is the handle of a knife, axe or tool

explanation.surface: A man is obliged to operate a particular component of a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters of CHAP MUST, giving CAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating shaft carrying cams, as in a car engine, is a specific component of machinery.

clue.text: Most caring figure starts to drop everything and relax

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their first letters

parts.note: to rest is to relax

explanation.surface: The most caring person starts by dropping everything to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word meaning gentle and loving, so most caring.

clue.text: Holding outdoor activity around lake

indicators.note: the activity goes around the lake

parts.note: camping is an outdoor activity

explanation.surface: Holding an outdoor camping trip around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Clutching firmly, gripping, is holding something tight.

clue.text: Warm trio of islands to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going westward means reading right to left

parts.note: three islands: Elba, I (island) and Cos, the Greek isle also spelt Kos

explanation.surface: Three islands lying westward enjoy a warm climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warm' looks like temperature, but it is friendly; COS + I + ELBA read westward.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm person is friendly and outgoing, enjoying company, which is the sense here.

clue.text: Trim graduate climbing hill-range

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upward

parts.note: BA is the Bachelor of Arts degree
a ridge is a long range of hills

explanation.surface: A slim graduate is climbing a range of hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' looks like an adjective, slim, but it is the verb: to shorten a text.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a book or text by cutting is to trim it.

clue.text: Geographical feature seen in Tuscany only

indicators.note: the letters can be seen within the run of these words

explanation.surface: A landscape feature that is found only in Tuscany.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep gorge carved by a river is a landform, an example of a geographical feature.

clue.text: Mother possessed by a spirit that's wicked

indicators.note: possessed means held inside, so the mother goes within

parts.note: zing is spirit, energy
ma is a mother

explanation.surface: A mother possessed by a wicked spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' looks like evil, but it is the slang sense: excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang wicked means excellent or wonderful, so an approving synonym.

clue.text: Daze from port drunk with us

indicators.note: drunk means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daze brought on by drinking port with us.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of near-unconsciousness, being dazed and confused.

clue.text: Expert with good month to review app, perhaps

parts.note: a pro is an expert

indicators.note: reviewing means looking back, so the month is read backwards

parts.note: Mar is the abbreviation for March

explanation.surface: A specialist with a good month is set to assess a mobile app.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling is the computing one.
explanation.definitionFit: An app is one kind of computer software, so the 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Sauce is something unwelcome on duck

parts.note: a pest is something unwelcome, a nuisance
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A sauce is unwelcome when poured on duck.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian sauce of basil, garlic and pine nuts is a kind of sauce.

clue.text: Sandwich and wine consumed in part of golf club

indicators.note: the wine goes inside the other piece, as if swallowed by it

parts.note: the toe is the end of a golf club's head furthest from the shaft
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Lunch at the golf clubhouse: a sandwich and some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' suggests the clubhouse, but it is the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A toasted sandwich, often with cheese, is a British snack.

clue.text: Craft in English river capsized

indicators.note: in a down clue, capsized means turned over, read upward

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: A boat in an English river has capsized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat, but it is a trade, a skilled occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled occupation or line of work, such as a carpenter's, is a craft.

clue.text: Swimmer is one taking over from ace in team

indicators.note: one letter replaces another, taking its place

parts.note: a squad is a team
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sporting swimmer who joins the team in place of its star.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea creature with ten arms moves through the water, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Secretly chummy with soldier

parts.note: to be in with someone is to be friendly with them
a private is a soldier of the lowest rank

explanation.surface: A man is quietly on friendly terms with a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something away from others, unseen, is doing it confidentially.

clue.text: Too keen again, agree to change

parts.note: over means again, as in do it over

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone excessively enthusiastic once more agrees to make a change.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively keen or zealous, the eagerness pushed beyond what is wanted.

clue.text: Visitor shot short host at the end

indicators.note: short means the word is missing its last letter

parts.note: a shot, as in a shot in the dark, is a guess

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A visitor shoots a host who was too short, at the end of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a verb; it is the noun, an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone staying at another's home or attending an event is a visitor.
